method: Moving AVG() with a ROWS frame
syntax: AVG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY device ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
summary: An aggregate window with a bounded ROWS frame can summarize a moving set of neighboring records without collapsing rows.
documentation: An aggregate window with a bounded ROWS frame can summarize a moving set of neighboring records without collapsing rows. A one-preceding frame averages the current row and at most one previous row within the device partition.
inputs: readings(id INTEGER, device TEXT NOT NULL, value INTEGER), with distinct ids.
returns: id, device and moving_average, ordered by device then id.
caution: ROWS counts records, not elapsed days or a numeric distance in the ordering key. AVG ignores NULL values and returns NULL when every value in the current frame is NULL.
scenarios: Smooth a local sequence of sensor observations over two records.
Show a small moving average beside ordered report rows.
Compare recent measurements without merging separate devices.
title: Average the latest two records
problem: Return id, device and AVG(value) over the current and immediately preceding row of each device AS moving_average. Order device rows by id and output by device, id. Preserve AVG’s NULL behavior.
hint: Use ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW rather than an unbounded frame.
goal: Use Moving AVG() with a ROWS frame or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
